about: Look blocks that cannot be switched on over a finished picture: they need the game's objects, materials or camera built for them. A vibe lists them under "upgrade". Where a light version exists as a look, "lite" names it.

upgrades.gives: the full risograph print: every object printed in its own spot ink by role, with ink sets and screen signals
upgrades.why: Objects get ROLES instead of colours and are drawn into a special buffer; the game must ask for every material by role.

upgrades.gives: true pixel art: a camera snapped to whole pixels, objects lit through hand-made colour ramps, sprites drawn in code
upgrades.why: It needs its own orthographic camera, its own materials on every object and no tone mapping.

upgrades.gives: the whole 90s console pipeline: warping textures on your models, 4:3 letterbox, eyes-closed, flash and dread effects
upgrades.why: The retro-console look already uses its vertex wobble; the texture warp needs models cut into small pieces and its screen effects need game code to drive them.

upgrades.gives: three-tone toon materials, ink bleeding in when hurt, and colour sets that cross-fade between levels or times of day
upgrades.why: The ink look already uses its line and hatching pass; the rest is materials and game events.

upgrades.gives: materials repainted in flat pigment, strokes that stay on the walls, a painted sky, and two more styles with a live switch
upgrades.why: The painterly look uses its finishing brush; the rest patches every material and replaces the sky.

upgrades.gives: focus on your own subject, camera shots (flyover, podium, diorama), ambient occlusion and a night grade
upgrades.why: The toy look already uses its lens; the rest needs the game to say what to focus on and when.

upgrades.gives: the haze itself in the air of the world, a sky that melts into it, cloud shadows and a matching light rig
upgrades.why: The soft-haze look uses its final grade; the air replaces the starter's fog and sky, which is a change to the world.

upgrades.gives: real photographic rendering: one real sky lighting everything, soft shadows, reflections, depth of field, auto exposure
upgrades.why: It needs scanned assets, a sky image, its own lights and two extra npm packages; the film look only grades the picture.

upgrades.gives: a world that is painted in watercolour as you walk through it
upgrades.why: The paint lives in the world's own materials and a map of where the player has been.

upgrades.gives: a world made of thick oil-paint dabs pinned to things
upgrades.why: Everything is rebuilt out of brush dabs; there is no ordinary scene to draw over.

upgrades.gives: a world shaded in coloured-pencil strokes that follow each form
upgrades.why: Each surface needs its own pencil material and stroke directions.

upgrades.gives: a world sewn from cloth, with seams, stitches and felt
upgrades.why: It is a way of building the world (quilts, stuffed shapes), not a way of drawing one.

upgrades.gives: a whole painted valley with its own sky, clouds, grass and hours
upgrades.why: It is a complete place with its own render pipeline, not a style for another game.
